name: NVIDIA Corp

Dip-buyers edged the session; the week, though, belonged to the bears.

Wall Street is still Strong Buy with a ~$305 average target (~48% upside). BUY at medium conviction — scale in rather than chase — because the only real risk here is valuation/multiple compression, and the stock just fell 7 of 10 sessions. analysis:
## The reset, in context

NVIDIA just gave back about **13% from its May 14 record of $235.47**, closing Friday at $205.10 after a [−6.2% session](https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/NVDA/forecast/) and a week that was red 7 days out of 10. The important point: **nothing in the business broke**. This was a valuation cool-down in the most-owned stock on the planet, not a fundamental crack.

## Why the fundamentals say 'buy the dip'

The numbers are still extraordinary. FY26 revenue hit a record **$215.94B, up 65%**, with [data center growing ~69% and Blackwell sold out](https://intellectia.ai/blog/nvda-stock-earnings-analysis-may-2026). Management points to roughly **$1T of AI-chip demand through 2027 in confirmed orders**, and the [hyperscalers are set to spend $200B+ on AI infrastructure in 2026](https://intellectia.ai/blog/nvidia-stock-analysis-2026-ai-demand). On top of the data-center engine, NVIDIA is widening its TAM: the [RTX Spark 'superchip' pushes it into PCs](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/02/nvidias-new-pc-chips-are-ceos-bid-to-own-every-part-of-ai-stack.html), and today's **LG Group partnership** moves it into humanoid robots and physical AI.

## The catch: valuation

The single risk worth respecting is the multiple. At **~31x forward earnings and a ~$5T market cap**, NVDA prices in a lot of good news, and [any wobble in AI capex could trigger sharp compression](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/261505954-nvda-nvidia-stock-price-2026-2030-tradingkey). That's exactly why the call is BUY but **scaled** — a starter here, adds toward $200 and the 52-week trend, not a chase.

## What would change the call

A reclaim of **$218** confirms the dip is bought and reopens a run at the $235 high. A loss of **$200** turns this into a HOLD and a wait-for-the-base, with the high-$180s the next shelf. The Street, for what it's worth, is still **Strong Buy with a ~$305 average target** — roughly 48% above here.
